text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwqegian papers this morning:

- At the request of the European Council, the Ministry of Labour and Local Government has chosen to keep confidential a report on rasicm and intolerance in Norway until further notice. Amnesty International wants the report published now.
- Soer-Troendelag county wants to send 850 Norwegian patients to Sweden where hospital care is cheaper.

- Terje Roed Larsen, the former Middle East mediator who went home to become national planning minister before being forced out of office because of an old tax dispute, has decided to accept fines of 50,000 crowns. But he insists he is innocent.

- A majority in parliament warns against weakening regional bank Fokus Bank. Politicians say Norway needs a commercial bank outside the Oslo area and that a strong Fokus Bank is the best solution. Fokus Bank said on Monday it viewed a takeover bid by Sparebankgruppen, a group of savings banks, as hostile.
- Tor Laegereid, Managing director in Sparebankgruppen, says Sparebankgruppen will not raise the takeover bid for Fokus Bank if a competing bid is made.
- The Competition Authority may stop Sparebankgruppen's planned takeover of Fokus Bank. The reason is Sparebankgruppen would gain monopoly in several local markets.
- Sparebanken NOR, or Union Bank of Norway, is interested in Fokus Bank but has not decided whether to join the battle.
- Tiger Management will sell its 17 percent holding in Norway Seafood through a secondary placement at 55 crowns per share in connection with Norway Seafoods becoming listed on the Oslo Bourse.
- Both the Nordic countries as well as the rest of the EU are divided on whether to impose anti-dumping duties on Norwegian salmon imports.
